meta.mode_reason: Rich, verified, license-clean REAL campus imagery is registered for almost every named school in the story: 13 cover-able landscape backgrounds (6 Scout sct_ + 7 Designer des_, all with complete license+identity), well above the >=5 floor. Every beat's named cast (ETH / MIT / Stanford / Peking / Tsinghua / Michigan / Caltech / UCL / Princeton / Washington) has a real photograph that honestly belongs, so no generative or data_driven fallback is warranted. Backgrounds are drawn ONLY from designer.json meta.team_brief.cinematic_cover_able_backgrounds; every image/video media_ref resolves to a registered sct_/des_ id (never a bare Detective ref_ or the cinematic_imagery_manifest scratchpad).
meta.engine_note: Copy the exact CSS/JS technique from cinematographer/references/example_cinematic_scroll.html (pinned .cin-stage full-bleed layer; one .cin-bg per scene crossfaded by a CSS `transition:opacity ~1.15s ease` toggled `.active` via an IntersectionObserver on the text beats at rootMargin '-45% 0px -45% 0px'; decoding=async + img.decode() pre-decode; gentle ken-burns via a CSS transform transition on `.active`, NEVER a forced-reflow restart). Apply the blog's OWN editorial_dark theme (bg ~#0e0f13, gilt-gold accent #e3b23c, teal referee #5aa9b5, Didot display / Georgia body) — not the example's mint/Georgia demo palette.
meta.scene_arc: ETH night hero (cin_00) -> MIT night, QS's champion (edt_01) -> Stanford Oval, the tight summit anchor (edt_02) -> Peking, the swinger (edt_03) -> quiet hold on Peking for the weighting-mechanics beat (edt_04, REST) -> Tsinghua, reputation-lifted (edt_05) -> Princeton, the neutral 'you decide' centerpiece (edt_06) -> Michigan, the referee's output giant (edt_07) -> Caltech, the small-dense riser (edt_08) -> quiet hold on Caltech for the validation beat (edt_09, REST) -> UCL, a human-scale 'find yourself' campus (edt_10) -> ETH night reprise/bookend for the close (edt_11) -> Washington, a quiet methods-appendix backdrop (edt_12). Night/dusk shots (ETH, MIT) anchor the nocturne palette; the ETH bookend ties the film back to its opening.
meta.rest_policy_check: 2 rest scenes, non-consecutive (cin_04 then a fresh cin_05; cin_09 then a fresh cin_10). Zero kind:gradient/color scenes exist (photographic mode) — every rest HOLDS a real photo dimmed/framed under a heavier scrim, never a black gradient gap (PIT-54). Each rest re-uses the immediately-prior verified photo as a calmer hold of the SAME surface (edt_04 holds Peking from edt_03; edt_09 holds Caltech from edt_08).
meta.unused_note: des_img_berkeley (Campanile) and sct_tokyo (Yasuda Auditorium) are registered and cover-able but not needed as distinct cinematic beats (one background per beat, and closer-fitting subjects were chosen). They remain available to the Designer as in-body section images for edt_03 (Berkeley, the reverse-direction swinger) and the swinger/reputation set (Tokyo). Not using every registered asset is fine; every asset that IS staged resolves to a registered id.
meta.logos_excluded: des_crest_harvard / des_crest_oxford / des_crest_cambridge are LOGOS (coats of arms), not landscape backgrounds — never used as cinematic backgrounds (they are optional inline champion marks for the Programmer).

background.treatment: Full-bleed cover of the animated ETH Zurich Hauptgebaude night panorama (a real Wikimedia photograph with an ffmpeg Ken-Burns push-in + warm-light breathing boomerang added; not AI video, no person). This IS the cin_00 layer of the pinned .cin-stage, lifted above the stage's global darkening (higher z-index) so the hero keeps its own brightness. The hero's furniture (headline, kicker, stat strip, scrim, vignette) lives in a SEPARATE transparent overlay in <main> that scrolls OVER this fixed backdrop.

cin_00.transition_in: None on entry (active by default from the very top, before any scroll). The SAME crossfade engine carries cin_00 -> cin_01: when edt_01 crosses the viewport middle the IntersectionObserver toggles .active from cin_00 to cin_01, dissolving the ETH night hero into the MIT night background as one continuous move (no 'cover ends, content begins' seam).
cin_00.overlay_dissolve: The transparent hero overlay (furniture only) OPACITY-DISSOLVES (opacity 1 -> 0) as it scrolls out, driven by a small rAF scroll handler or CSS scroll-out. OPACITY ONLY — never scale the transparent overlay (scaling a transparent pane re-introduces the seam). Under prefers-reduced-motion the overlay stays static + fully opaque and never touches the video.
cin_00.scrim: Solid dark headline plate over the black night-sky band + a subtle vignette (the Hero role's furniture), tuned to hold WCAG AA over the night image. linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(10,11,15,.55) 0%, rgba(10,11,15,.20) 42%, rgba(10,11,15,.88) 100%) as the base stage scrim.
cin_00.motion: The clip's own seamless boomerang (a centered ~12% push-in toward the lit dome + gentle warm-light breathing). Do NOT add a second ken-burns transform on top of the video. Reduced-motion / JS-off / no-video: show the poster still assets/teaser.jpg (already always in the DOM per the Hero build_contract).
cin_00.source_credit: Photo: Nemanja Skoric / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0) - ETH Zurich Hauptgebaude, identity verified. Motion = a camera push-in + light animation added to the still (not AI video, not a person).
cin_00.verify_note: Tag cin_00 data-cin + data-des='des_hero_video' for background traceability, but the hero's clickable Verify hit stays on the .teaser OVERLAY (data-des='des_hero_video', class-marker 'teaser') per hero.json.verify — NOT on the cin_00 backdrop layer. The .cin-stage wrap auto-excludes the cover from the Verify engine (isDecorative).

global.engine: A single pinned full-bleed background layer (.cin-stage, position:fixed inset:0 z-index:0) behind the text column (main position:relative z-index:1). One .cin-bg layer per scene, stacked; the active scene has opacity 1, the rest 0, crossfaded by a CSS `transition:opacity ~1.15s ease` on the .active class (NOT a JS opacity tween, NOT a keyframe restart). An IntersectionObserver on the text beats (rootMargin '-45% 0px -45% 0px', threshold 0) toggles .active on the .cin-bg whose data-cin matches the beat whose middle crosses the viewport middle. cin_00 is .active by default from the top. Ken-burns is a CSS transform transition on .active (scale 1.0 -> ~1.03/1.05); NEVER force a synchronous reflow (no `void el.offsetWidth`) to restart animation. Copy the exact CSS/JS from references/example_cinematic_scroll.html; apply the blog's editorial_dark theme + these verified images.
global.hero_handoff: cin_00 (the ETH hero video) is the FIRST .cin-bg layer inside the same .cin-stage, lifted above the stage darkening so it keeps full brightness, and .active by default. Its interactive furniture (headline, kicker, stat strip, scrim, vignette) lives in a SEPARATE transparent overlay in <main> that scrolls OVER the fixed cin_00 backdrop and OPACITY-DISSOLVES (opacity only, never scale) as it scrolls out. The same IntersectionObserver crossfade carries cin_00 -> cin_01 when edt_01 centres, so the hero-to-content transition is seamless. The hero's Verify hit stays on the .teaser overlay (data-des='des_hero_video'), not on cin_00.
global.reduced_motion: Under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): disable parallax, ken-burns, crossfade and video autoplay. Render each scene's background as a STATIC, scrimmed per-section still (the framed rests show their dimmed still; cin_00 shows the poster assets/teaser.jpg). The whole story reads and makes its point with motion fully off. This is NOT an off switch - the imagery and the stage stay; only motion freezes.
global.no_toggle_guardrail: The cinematic stage is UNCONDITIONAL. Do NOT emit any on/off toggle, `.cinematic-off` / `html.cinematic` class gate, or sessionStorage state. Cinematic CSS is always on; the only adaptation is prefers-reduced-motion (which freezes motion, not the stage).
global.performance: Lazy-load every scene background (loading='lazy' or IO-gated src swap); decode only the current + next pair; put decoding='async' on every background and call img.decode() on load to pre-decode (kills crossfade stutter). Mobile: serve a smaller srcset per background and default the hero to its poster still (assets/teaser.jpg); never decode 13 full-res images at once. Animate transform/opacity only (compositor); rAF-throttle the scroll handler; never animate layout properties. Virality happens on mobile - keep total weight low (web .webp backgrounds; hero webm 0.44 MB + mp4 1.23 MB).
global.readability: Every text-over-background scene gets a per-scene background scrim (above). ADDITIONALLY the body prose in <main> that scrolls over the always-on dark stage needs its own frosted dark backplate: main>section:not(.teaser):not(.refs){ background:rgba(13,11,8,~.6); backdrop-filter:blur(~3px) } at the PROSE width - wide charts/maps/card-decks break OUT as their own frosted figure, but wide data-grid tables stay within the backplate measure. Text-shadow alone is not enough on the dark stage. Tune alpha up on the two rests and the appendix (heavier scrims).
global.verifiability: Every image/video background's media_ref resolves to a registered Scout sct_ or Designer des_ item (verified license + identity) - never a bare Detective ref_ or the cinematic_imagery_manifest scratchpad. The Programmer tags each background data-cin + data-sct (sct_ backgrounds: cin_06/cin_10/cin_11/cin_12) or data-des (des_ backgrounds: cin_00/cin_01/cin_02/cin_03/cin_04/cin_05/cin_07/cin_08/cin_09) so validate.py Section 6 checks its license + identity. Decorative background imagery gets aria-hidden / empty alt, but the visible per-scene source credit stays in the DOM. The page is fully usable with JS off (static per-section stills, never a blank column).
global.centerpiece_scene: cin_06 - hosts the Interaction centerpiece int_01 / des_reweighter (edt_06). The widget keeps its own provenance id (data-des='des_reweighter'); the background carries data-cin + data-sct='sct_princeton' independently. Calm background motion + strong scrim so the explorable is the focus.
